findings.claim: The decisive 'existing browser convention' evidence cites a spec file that is not verified anywhere in the packet, so the judge cannot confirm the claimed viewport/scrollWidth pattern exists.
findings.evidence: analysis.md states: "Existing browser convention: `a11y-responsive-certification.spec.ts:65,96-99` sets a viewport and compares document `scrollWidth` with `window.innerWidth`", but `cited_paths` contains no EXISTS entry for `a11y-responsive-certification.spec.ts`, and the file_tree lists only `./frontend/e2e` (unexpanded) and `./frontend/playwright.accessibility.config.ts` — the spec file itself never appears. This is the same evidence-invisibility defect class the artifact itself flags as `gap-review-packet-evidence-integrity`.
findings.suggested_fix: Add an EXISTS check for `a11y-responsive-certification.spec.ts` and quote the actual lines 65 and 96-99 (setViewportSize call and scrollWidth/innerWidth assertion) into the 'Evidence excerpts supplied to review' section.

findings.claim: The claim that three existing components use Tailwind `@container` classes is supported only by file-existence checks, not by any quoted source, so the 'established local convention' premise of the ADOPT verdict for cand-001 is unverifiable in-packet.
findings.evidence: analysis.md asserts: "`frontend/src/components/assistant-ui/enhanced-thread.tsx:110`, `frontend/src/components/ui/card.tsx:28`, and `frontend/src/components/ui/field.tsx:44` already use Tailwind `@container` classes." `cited_paths` proves only that the three files exist; no excerpt of the alleged `@container` class usage is quoted, unlike the `ai-settings-panels.tsx:184` line which is quoted in full.
findings.suggested_fix: Quote the exact class strings from each of the three files at the cited line numbers, mirroring the treatment given to `ai-settings-panels.tsx:184`.

findings.claim: cand-005's Tier 2 evidence cites the wrong documentation page for the claim it supports.
findings.evidence: cand-005 evidence entry uses `source_url: ".../src/docs/place-content.mdx"` with the claim "Official Tailwind documentation demonstrates arbitrary grid-template column values using grid-cols-[repeat(...)]" — `place-content` documents content placement, not `grid-cols` arbitrary values; the supporting doc would be the grid-template-columns page.
findings.suggested_fix: Re-cite the Tailwind `grid-template-columns` documentation (grid-cols.mdx) for the arbitrary grid template claim, or correct the claim to match what place-content.mdx actually documents.
